REcoMMENDATION No. 9

mutual agreement the city took over the cemetery as an historical land.mark. On the other hand should a lodge be relieved of its obligation merely because lack of interest and poor management has forced
them into a position wherein the lodge must use some of its own funds
to rehabilitate the cemetery or are they to be permitted to slide o~t
from under by forming a cemetery district which will assume their
responsibilities.
Your committee questions the use of public funds as a means of
relieving us of our obligation. We wonder at the reaction of a brother
or his family in the purchase of a plot in a Masonic cemtery, when
they suddenly find that the cemetery has become, not a Masonic plot,
but one supported and managed by public funds.
Your committee on Masonic Cemeteries therefore recommends:
1. That legislation be prepared to clarify Section 333h of the
California Masonic Code by setting forth conditions under which a
lodge may "relieve itself of its trust obligations."
2. Should this Grand Lodge determine that some or all of our
Masonic cemeteries are operating in violation of our rulings on commercialism, then legislation should be prepared requiring all of our
cemeteries to operate within the terms of such ruling or to dispose of
their holding through cemetery districts or otherwise.
RECOMMENDATION No. 8
MASONIC PLOTS WITHIN PRIVATE CEMETERIES

Your Committee on Masonic Cemeteries has found that Masonic
plots within private cemeteries have been and are being kept in excellent
condition. As long as a private cemetery displays the proper respect
in the use of our name, we realize that there is little to be done.
The mere fact that a private cemetery has a Masonic section (usually not exclusively sold to Masons) may in itself indicate that our
name is being used in fostering the sale of their lots. This custom,
however, is one of long standing and no breach of our laws has come
to the attention of this committee.
With this generally accepted practice of Masonic plots within
private cemeteries, your committee believes that proper legislation
should be provided prior to the time that conflict with our standards
might develop.
Your Committee on Masonic Cemeteries therefore recommends:
1. That legislation be presented to Grand Lodge for its consideration wherein the use of the name Masonic by private cemeteries would
be protected by a set of standards as to the use of our name as well
as setting a minimum standard for the maintenance and perpetual
care of the Masonic plot.
2. That should such legislation be the pleasure of Grand Lodge,
then all private cemeteries be sent copies of such legislation.

Your Committee on Masonic Cemeteries has information on nine
cemeteries where a Masonic Lodge has ownership jointly with the
lndepend~n~ Order of Odd Fellows. One of this group has a cemetery
operated Jointly by the community, the Masonic Lodge, the Independent Order of Odd Fellows and the Catholic Church through a board
of directors.
. Two of the abo:'~ now indicate that they are within a cemetery district. O.f the r~ain.ing seven cemeteries, one is neglected, two report
that their condition 1s very poor, two indicate that they are well cared
for and two have given the committee no report as to the condition
of their cemetery.
It .is the opinion .of your committee that joint ownership of a cemet~ry is not conduove to good maintenance. With the passage of
time, one or both organizations are apt to lose interest and live in
~ope that the other. will. pick up the full responsibility. Two organizations may enact legislation and, though well intended, may stir up misunderstandings and may even lead to hard feelings.
Your Committee on Masonic Cemeteries therefore recommends:
1. That legislation be prepared to prohibit any further joint ownership of cemetery property.
2. This legislation should permit a Masonic Lodge to own outright a~y property within a cemetery and the section belonging to a
Masonic Lodge should be their exclusive responsibility.
3. Cemeteries now under joint ownership should be encouraged
to secure clear title to that portion used by them and to sever the relationship of joipt ownership either through mutual agreement or by
purchase.
RECOMMENDATION No.

1O

MASONIC EMBLEMS ON SINGLE GRAVES

Your Committee on Masonic Cemeteries believes that the most
difficult problem before it is the great number of single graves that
have come to our attention all bearing some type of Masonic emblem
on their markers. Some are simple wooden markers with the emblem
painted thereo~ while other ar~ elaborate in their carving on marble.
A~l cemeteries seem to contain some of these Masonic graves. Some
~re single graves in lonely out of the way places, while others are
in small groups away from any recognized cemetery. In many of the
cases which we have studied, the graves are neglected and almost
forgotten.
It is the opinion of the Cemetery Committee that our obligation is
as great to the Mason buried in these graves as it is to the Mason
who happens to .be buried withi~ the limits of a Masonic cemetery.
Your Committee on Masonic Cemeteries therefore recommends:
1. That Grand Lodge determine our obligation to those Masons

existing cemeteries or in single isolated graves.
.

Masonic identification. Were we to attempt to locate and care for
all Masonic graves, our search would be limitless and we could never
be sure that our task was completed.

REPORT OF SPECIAL COMMITTEE TO
STUDY CLUBHOUSES
To the Most Worshipful Grand Lodge, F. & A. M., State of California:
At the annual.communication of 1957 there was adopted a resolution
directing the Grand Master to appoint a special committee to make a
study of the Masonic Clubhouses at the University of California at
Berkeley and at Los Angeles. This resolution was passed as a result
of the recommendations by the Grand Master in his annual report to
Grand Lodge.
By letter dated May 20, 1958, two committees were appointed. One
to study the clubhouse at Berkeley and the other to study the clubhouse
in Los Angeles.
The reason for requesting a report was the feeling that Grand Lodge
exercised little or no control over the activities of these two clubhouses,
even though costs of supervision, operation and maintenance are budgeted Grand Lodge expense items. The expenese of operating the two
clubhouses is approximately $35,000.00 per year.
Each of your special committees has prepared and filed reports covering their findings. These reports should have further study by the Jurisprudence and Policy and General Purposes Committees.
A summary of the conclusions reached is as follows:
Insofar as the Berkeley Clubhouse is concerned. that section of the

260

PROCEEDING S OF THE

committee recommends that no action on the part of Grand Lodge is
necessary or required, for under the Articles of Incorporatio n and the
By-Laws by which that Board of Directors operate, Grand Lodge and
the Grand Master have all the control that should be necessary for the
following reasons:
1. The Articles of Incorporatio n state specifically that the Corporation shall operate in accordance with the rules, regulations and discipline
of Grand Lodge and shall always be subject to such rules and regulations.
2. That the Directors shall be appointed in the manner required by
the rules and regulations of Grand Lodge.
3. That the student organization operates under a constitution which
appears to be compatible with the purposes of the clubhouse.
As might be expected, the conclusions by the southern section of
your committee differ somewhat from those of the northern section and
may be summarized as follows:
1. A complete set of legal papers pertaining to the corporation governing the clubhouse at Los Angeles and the by-laws by which it is
operated are not on fl.le in the office of the Grand Secretary or obtainable
from the Board of Directors. It is the recommendation of the committee
that a complete set be fl.led.
2. Title to the real property should be vested in Grand Lodge.
3. Some recommendations have been made in regard to the composition and term of office of the Board of Directors.
4. Further recommendations stress the need for improved communi·
cations regarding the clubhouse facilities and services among the members of the constituent lodges.·
Respectfully submitted,
PAUL A. BROM, (Northern Section)
FRED H. BLANCHARD , (Southern Section)

REPOR T OF THE BOARD OF DIREC TORS OF THE
MASON IC CLUB HOUSE, BERKELEY
To the Most Worship ful Grand Lodge, F. & A. M .. State of California:

The Board of Directors of the Masonic Club of the University, Inc.,
Berkeley. is pleased to submit its Annual Report of the activities of the
Club House for the fiscal year ended July 31. 1958.
The year has been an active one insofar as stude~t act.ivities ~re
concerned; however. your Board has given serious considerati~n during
the year to ways and means of encouraging and promoting an increased
use of the club by a greater number of qualified students on the ca~pus.
A committee of the Board is making a careful study of the operat~onal
program of the Club House and a preliminary report of the committee,
which includes a number of recommendations, has been accepted by
the Board. We expect to have in operation at the beginni? g of the fall
semester an operatin g plan that will encourage more qualified students
to affiliate themselves with the Club House and participa te in the activi~
ties which it sponsors. In carrying the plan into effect, a number of
student-i mposed initiation requirements that have g~o~n up over the
years are being modified or eliminated. The supervision of the Club

GRAND LODGE OP CALIFORNIA

263

House, which has been lacking in many respects due to lack of
sufficient quali.6ed personnel, will be improved. To accomplish this, it
is planned that a trained social activities supervisor will be substitut ed
for the student assistant and. by this measure, it is hoped that the social
activities program of the students can be better planned and directed
and the effectiveness of our Executive Director can thereby be supplemented and enhanced. This program will entail a somewh at greater
expendit ure for salaries than has been required in the past and our
budget for the fiscal year ending July 31, 1959 has been increased in
the salaries category by $750.00 and for promotional activities by
$500.00. It is expected that this increase of $1250.00 in our budget for
this program will result in needed improvement in supervision of the
Club House, provide guidance to the students in the planning of their
social activities. and, it is hoped, will encourag e use of the Club House
by an increased number of quali.6ed Universi ty students.
The Club House serves as a home away from home for our many
young Universi ty affiliated Masons. It is a great gatherin g place
especially at noon. Our guest book shows that an increasing number
of visitors to Berkeley stop in to see the Club House. In addition to
serving the students , the Club House facilities have been extended
during the year to organiza tions such as the Henry Morse Stephen s
Lodge, the East Bay Masters and Warden s Association. the Universi ty
Service Club, the District Supervisors of De Molay, and other Masonic
District Officers Associations.
The Board has approved the banks in which monies of the Club
House are to be deposite d with the further provision that no deposit in
any one of sucb depositories shall exceed the amount therein insured by
the Federal Deposit Insuranc e Corporat ion. Savings account transfers
were made during the year to comply with this new policy.
Damage of $739.00 to the property caused by an automobile accident
was fully covered by insurance. Restorat ion was completed and insurance recovery received during the year.
There have been no major replacements of property during the year.
However, extensive repairs are now being made to replace cast stone
caps over windows on the exterior of the building. Water damage over
the years caused the cast stone caps, which were installed at the time
the building was construc ted, to chip and fall apart. Sections of stone
falling to the ground caused a hazard. This work should be completed
by the time school commences this fall.
A study is being ~ade of the use of the student loan fund with the
objective of encouraging greater use of the loan fund by students in
qualified cases.
During the year we accepted with regrets the resignation from our
Board of Brother Walter T. Helms. Walter asked to be relieved because
of pressure of personal activities. He was succeeded on the Board by

This committee was appointed to make a study relative to the use
of slides, charts and other visual aids in connection with our ritual.
(Proceedings 1957, page 387).
Our first problem was to determine what visual aids could be used
under the long~established law and policy of this Grand Lodge.
One of the recognized landmarks is "the secrecy of the institution.''
( C.M.C., App. p. 343). In 1908, this Grand Lodge adopted a clear
declaration as to the secrecy of its ritualistic work, which w:e regard as
binding upon us. ( 1908: 120). This declaration included the following
points:
"1. Freemasonry has as essentials certain secrets of ritual which it
forever conceals and never reveals to any person in the world except its
own members.
"2. These ancient mysteries are communicated only by the instruc~
tive tongue to the attentive ear and are safely lodged in the faithful
breast; and any other mode of communication in Ancient Craft Masonry
is most positively forbidden in solemn form and manner.
"3. So likewise is forbidden the writing, printing or marking in any
manner, whereby the same becomes legible or intelligible to any person,
lest these secrets might become known to the profane.
4. No individual Mason is exempt from the obligation of profound
secrecy, and no human power can authorize him to write, print or mark
Masonic secrets in any manner whatsoever.
"5. The secrets are ancient landmarks of Freemasonry, and no body
of men, inside or outside of Lodge or Grand Lodge, has power to make
innovations in Ancient Craft Masonry.
"It is no excuse or justification for any that men are eager to break
these laws, or that men have broken them before, or that in other degrees
or orders of American Masonry cipher rituals may be in common use.
Our duty and obligation, as Ancient Craft Masons compel our obedience
to these ancient regulations."
This same policy was followed in 1938 ( 1938: 33~34) in the approval
of a ruling by Grand Lecturer Leslie E. Wood, as follows:
"Any slide, map, chart or picture of any nature, showing in part
or in whole, the secret work of the three degrees of Masonry, is contrary
to the laws of the fraternity and in violation of the obligations of the
order, and no lodge in this jurisdiction shall use such equipment in any
way, nor shall it or any Mason be in possession thereof."
It is settled, therefore, that -graphical references to or portrayals of
the secret or esoteric portions of our work are contrary to our laws and
obligations, whether by way of writings, codes or ciphers, or by slides,
films, charts, pictures or carvings. Consequently, our study of visual aids

REPORT OF COMMITTEE ON GRIEVANCES

At 1 :30 P.M. Grand Lodge was called on, the Grand Master presiding.
The invocation was delivered by the Grand Chaplain.

REPORT OF SPECIAL COMMITTEE ON SCHOLARS.HIPS
To the Most Worshipful Grand Lodge, F. & A. M., State of California:

The special committee appointed by the Grand Master to consider
the question of continuing the program of awarding scholarships for
advanced study in higher education, as recommended by Grand Master
L. Harold Anderson (Proceedings 1957, page 74), has had one meeting
in 1958. The committee submits the following report and recommendations:
1. The scholarship program as originally conceived is a worthwhile
activity in furthering Grand Lodge support of free public education,
and should be continued.
2. Indifferent results during the past years have been due to inadequate publicity and to failure on the part of applicants to comply with
announced standards.
3. Publicity for the program should be given through the constituent
lodges, as well as through university and college channels heretofore
used.
4. Exact standards should be set up for qualification and no consideration given to applicants and submissions which do not conform thereto.
5. Included in the specifications should be the requirement that
papers submitted deal with the history, development and value of the
public school system; and that they be of general interest and suitable for
publication in whole or in part in the California Freemason.
6. That the incoming Grand Master appoint a Special Scholarship
Committee to administer the program, judge the entries and recommend
to the Grand Master the granting of awards. Copies of winning papers
should be circulated not only to all members of the special committee,
but also to the Grand Master in support of recommendations for awards,
and to others directly interested.
7. That the special committee so appointed secure all possible information from other Grand Jurisdictions concerning similar programs
which may be in effect.
8. That the sum of $2,000 be appropriated for the purpose of awarding two scholarships during the forthcoming year.
Respectfully submitted:
PHIL N. MYERS
HENRY C. CLAUSEN
JoE L. SHELL
VIERLING KERSEY

Referred to the Committee on Finance.

To the Most Worshipful Grand Lodge F. 8 A. M. of California:
Your Committee on Grievances reports as follows:
Our committee has considered 68 trial records, of which 32 will be
covered by this omnibus report and the others will be the subjects of
special reports by committee members. The special reports cover petitions for restoration, appeals, and any cases which seem to require
separate treatment.
We continue to urge those having anything to do with Masonic trials
or discipline in the lodges to carefully study the Masonic Code. When
it is read carefully its provisions are almost always plain and understandable. It would seem beneficial for the Masters and Secretaries to
look over the reports of this committee in the printed proceedings of
Grand Lodge for the past twenty years or so.
Secretaries should send copies of all charges filed with the lodge to
the Grand Secretary immediately so that Grand Lodge will know of
pending matters and also may tender some good advice as to any
defects of form of the charges. There is no present provision in our
law but it would seem desirable that a secretary notify the Grand Secretary whenever he mails a notice to anyone under Section 732, Masonic
Code, warning of automatic expulsion. He should enclose a copy of the
notice and state when it was sent by registered mail. As we stated in
our report last year, the secretary should make certain what prison or
jail the accused is in before mailing a notice under 732. Prisoners are
transferred from time to time.
Charges should be served strictly as required by our law. The same
applies to servlce of summons after a plea of Not Guilty is flied. If the
accused is within the jurisdiction of the lodge, i.e. living in the same
incorporated city, or living' nearer the lodge hall in unincorporated
territory than to the jurisduction of another lodge, service can be for
ten days and should be personal. If living in another city or town of this
state, service must be for thirty days and may be by mail. For those
without the state the time of service is ninety days. An amendment has
been proposed this year to make the ten-day service apply in the same
county, rather than within the jurisdiction of the lodge only. If such
change is made, the lodges should take note of it and govern themselves
accordingly.
If charges are served and the accused does not file a plea of Not
Guilty, and even where he flies a plea of Guilty, the Master must make
some investigation, and report in writing just what he did and what he
learned. The persons serving the charges should flle a certificate of
service and not leave it to the Master to state in his report that the
charges were served on a certain day, etc.
May we mention that Brother Ralph K. Pierson did not participate in
our deliberations on any trial record involving matters coming within

TRIAL RECORD NO. 1498
To the Most Worshipful Grand Lodge F. 8 A. M. of California:
A. L. S. was expelled by Lebanon Lodge No. 495 in 1956 after
conviction of a felony and commitment to a federal prison. Accused
now petitions for restoration, having completed his term and parole. His
petition was handed to the secretary of his former lodge on July 18,
1958, but could not be read to the lodge until its next stated meeting on
August 5. This was not sixty days prior to the opening of Grand Lodge
this year and the petition cannot be considered now. (See 767a,
Masonic Code). We offer the following resolution:

274

PROCEEDINGS OP THE

RESOLVED, that the Petition for Restoration of A. L. S. in Trial
Record No. 1498 be continued for consideration at the 1959 annual
communication of Grand Lodge, but that no further notice need be
given, and that a copy of this report be transmitted to petitioner and to
Lebanon Lodge.
Adopted.

TRIAL RECORD NO. 1514
To the Most Worshipful Grand Lodge F. & A. M. of California:
This is a petition for restoration.
L. R. M., a member of Metropolitan Lodge No. 646, was ordered
expelled from all the rights and privileges of Masonry by this Grand
Lodge at its last Communication for having committed Grand Theft of
the sum of approximately $269,000.00.
This petition is based primarily upon the fact that since petitioner's
expulsion the superior court in which he was tried and placed on probation made an order revoking his probation, then sentenced him to the
county jail for one year, suspended execution of this sentence, restored
him to probation, set aside the judgment of conviction, permitted him to
enter a plea of Not Guilty. terminated his probation and dismissed the
case. There is nothing to indicate that the court's action was based upon
any idea that he was not guilty of the theft of the $269,000.00. The
evidence presented at his Masonic trial clearly established that accused
was guilty of theft in this amount.
Accused has expressed no remorse for his conduct and has made no
adequate showing of rehabilitation. We therefore offer the following
resolution :
RESOLVED: That the petition of L. R. M. for restoration to the
rights and privileges of Masonry be and it is hereby denied without
prejudice.

TRIAL RECORD NO. 1570
To the Most Worshipful Grand Lodge F. & A. M. of California:
M. F .• a member of Patterson Lodge No. 488, pleaded Guilty in
Superior Court to a charge of grand theft and was placed upon probation
and ordered to make restitution.
Masonic charges were preferred by the Junior Warden and duly
served upon the accused. No plea of Not Guilty having been ~led ~n
reply thereto, the Master, pursuant to Sections 692.1 et seq., Cahforn~a
Masonic Code, proceeded to investigate the charges. The .Master did
not consult the victim of the alleged theft, but flied a written report
with the Lodge stating that, while he could not acquit the accused
because of the plea of Guilty in the Superior Court, the accused had
already been punished enough: and the Master, further, ruled that the
accused was to continue in good standing as a member of the Lodge.
Under Section 692.4, California Masonic Code, the investigation
and findings by the Master constitute a form of trial. A failure to fix a
penalty after a finding of Guilty constitutes a mistrial ( Sec~on 721 m,
California Masonic Code.) The sentence, or penalty, following a finding of Guilty. must be one of the three penalties prescribed by Section
721, California Masonic Cde.
The case must be returned to the lodge for retrial. Your committee
therefore offers the following resolution:
RESOLVED: That Trial Record No. 1570 be remanded to
Patterson Lodge No. 488 for further, proper proceedings.
Adopted.

TRIAL RECORD NO. 1575
To the Most Worshipful Grand Lodge of California:
The accused P. C. P., a member of Redlands Lodge No. 300 was
charged with unmasonic conduct in two specifications:
1. That he had deserted his wife and two children:
2. That he was living as man and wife with a woman other than his
wife.
The accused lived outside the jurisdiction of the lodge but within the
State of California, so as to permit service of notice upon him by mail.
The notice of charges, however, was sent to the accused by registered
mail to be delivered to the addressee only. The notice was returned to
the Lodge by the postoffice department, unaccepted by the accused. It
is therefore established by the record that the accused did not receive
notice of the charges by mail.
No plea of not guilty having been 6.led by the accused, the Master
made a finding that he was guilty of the charges. and fixed the penalty
as expulsion
It has previously been held in trial record No. 1504 that the pro-

276

PROCEEDINGS OF THE

visions of Section 707 CMC (formerly 308 Ross Digest). authorizing
service of summons by mail. are not complied with when the summons
is sent by registered mail to be delivered to addressee only. and is not
accepted by the addressee.
We therefore offer the following resolution:
RESOLVED: That the action of Redlands Lodge No. 300 in
expelling P. C. P. be reversed, and set aside, and the matter be remanded
to the lodge for further proceedings under the California Masonic Code.
Adopted.

TRIAL RECORD NO. 1584
To the Most Worshipful Grand Lodge F. 6 A. M. of California:
L. K. B.. a member of Security Lodge No. 581, was charged with
unmasonic conduct in three specifications: one of petty theft. one of
grand larceny, and one of not revealing the latter on his application for
the degrees.
The charges were served upon the accused, by registered mail, at his
residence in Scottsdale, Arizona, thirty days prior to the time set for him
to file his plea. No plea having been filed, the Master proceeded, under
Section 692.4, California Masonic Code, to investigate. He, thereafter,
made findings of Guilty on all specifications and the charge, and sentenced the accused to expu'lsion.
Since Section 707, California Masonic Code, requires 90 days'
notice to an accused resident out of the jurisdiction. these proceedings
are defective, as only 30 days' notice was given.
Your committee offers the following resolution:
RESOLVED: That the Master's finding of Guilty on the three
specifications and of the charge be and they are hereby disapproved and
set aside, and that Trial Record No. 1584 be returned to Security Lodge
No. 581 for proper service of the charges and retrial.
Adopted.

TRIAL RECORD NO. 1587
To the Most Worshipful Grand Lodge of California:
0. G. P .• a member of Bell Lodge No. 483, was charged therein
with being a bartender. After proper service and trial he was found
Guilty and ordered suspended. The evidence amply justifies the finding
of Guilt. However, the only penalty for violation of Section 513,
Masonic Code, is expulsion and we must therefore raise the penalty in
this case. We offer the following resolution:
RESOLVED: That the findings of Guilt in Trial Record No. 1587
are approved and affirmed, but the penalty is raised to expulsion,
and the accused 0. G. P. is hereby expelled from the rights and privileges of Masonry.
Adopted.

TRIAL RECORD NO. 1595
To the Most Worshipful Grand Lodge F. 6 A. M. of California:
Accused, S. F .• is a member of Loyalty Lodge No. 529, and the
record shows that a certified copy of a judgment of conviction of a
felony was obtained by the lodge and a notice under Section 732,
Masonic Code, was mailed to him. There is no certificate of mailing but
the Master in his report to the lodge stated that a letter had been written
to the accused. The notice was dated June 1, 1957, and stated that the
accused would be expelled at the stated meeting on August 6, 1957.
The Master's statement is that the accused demanded a trial. Nothing
apparently was done towards having a trial, such as election of commissioners, and on October 15, 1957, the accused apparently wrote the
lodge withdrawing his demand for a trial. There is a copy of such a
letter in the trial record but it is not identified. The Master at the
November stated meeting declared the accused expelled.
This was not proper procedure. When the accused demanded a
trial and the noticed date of August 6th had passed, the power of the
lodge to declare the accused expelled expired. It is possible ~hat an
accused who is given notice under 732 and who demands a trial may
thereafter withdraw that demand and allow the expulsion to be declared
at the stated meeting mentioned in the notice to him, provided he makes
the withdrawal of demand for trial timely. There is no provision in our
law for the withdrawal of such demand for trial after it is once made
and better practice would be to proceed with a trial as soon as demand
is made. Certainly in this case where the withdrawal of demand was not
made until several months after the demand the lodge acquires no right
to "automatically" expel the member.
The minutes of the November stated meeting were faulty in that
they recite a trial and verdict of commissioners, which the record shows
was not a true statement.
·
The lodge must start proceedings again in this case and follow the
Masonic Code requirements. We offer the following resolution:
RESOLVED. that the purported expulsion of S. F. by Loyalty
Lodge No. 529 is reversed and set aside and the lodge is directed to
proceed against him as provided in the Masonic Code.
Adopted.

TRIAL RECORDS NOS. 1596 AND 1597
To the Most Worshipful Grand Lodge F. 6 A. M. of California:
F. F. P. and L.A. P .• who are natural brothers, and who were both
members of Alcatraz Lodge No. 244, were charged separately in the
lodge with violations of the Edict of Grand Master L. Harold Ande~son
concerning membership and activity in the Royal Order of Caritas.
Separate trials were had, but on the same evening, and the evidence
and procedure were practically identical in each case. Each accused

278

PROCEEDINGS OP THE

admitted being an officer of and active in the Caritas organization, but
denied the legality of the Grand Master's Edict, making the particular
point that Masonry was no longer a prerequisite in said Caritas order.
(The Grand Master had stated in his edict that such was the case.)
In reporting his edict to Grand Lodge in 1957, on page 86 of the Proceedings, the Grand Master stated that the abolition of the Masonic
prerequisite did not in any way change the reasons and justification for
his edict. The edict was approved by Grand Lodge.
The two accused brothers herein were found Guilty and ordered
suspended. The trial master did not submit the question of expulsion to
the trial commissioners before taking a vote on suspension. This was
improper. However, we feel that a deliberate violation of Masonic
law merits the penalty of expulsion. The evidence herein conclusively
supports the finding of guilt. The accused in each case has filed an
appeal, but nothing has been Bled in support of such appeals. We offer
the following resolution:
RESOLVED, that the .findings of Guilt in both Trial Records Nos.
1596 and 1597 be affirmed and approved but that the penalty be raised
to expulsion and that F. F. P. and L.A. P. be expelled from the rights
and privileges of ·Masonry.
Adopted.

AMENDMENT OF SECTION 692.4
The resolution of Brother Albert F. Ross relating to 692.4 C.M.C.
proposes that a copy of the Master's written report and findings anent
guilt or innocence be delivered to the accused, at his request, personally,
or sent to him by registered mail. This would breach the confidential
requirement of lodge records.
To accomplish the purpose of the resolution, we move as follows:
RESOLVED, That Section 692.4 C.M.C. be amended to read as
follows:
Sec. 692.4. If, within the time limited in said notice, the accused
shall not have filed in writing, with the Secretary of the Lodge, his plea
of not guilty, the Master of said Lodge shall make a complete investigation and determine whether the charge and specifications are true, causing the facts relating thereto to be reduced to writing, in triplicate: and
he shall make findings as to the guilt or innocence of the accused, fix the
penalty therefor, and cause two ( 2) copies of the complete written record
to be forwarded to the Grand Secretary and one copy thereof to be filed
in the archives of the Lodge. At the next stated meeting of the Lodge
he shall announce his findings and the penalty imposed by him. Notice
of the penalty fixed by the Master shall be mailed to the accused at his
last known address.
Comment: The changes made by this amendment are as follows:
1. The word "quadruplicate " in line five is changed to "triplicate."
2. The language after the word "Lodge" in the ninth line, quoted
below, is stricken: " ... and one copy to be mailed to the accused at
his last known address."
3. The last sentence is added.
Adopted by 5/ 6 vote.

DECISION No. 4
By Decision No. 4 the Grand Master held that the individual members of a committee appointed to investigate an objection made to the
advancement of a candidate may make separate reports at the same or
different meetings.
Your committee holds that one report only may be filed and at one
stated meeting (California Masonic Code, Section 543). although the
report may contain findings concurred in by all or less than all of the
committee.
Adopted.

DECISION No. 19

The Grand 'M aster's Decision No. 19 would appear to be incorrect
for the following reasons:
1. Sec. 517-s, California Masonic Code, was adopted by a 5/6
vote in 1957 following a report based on 517-c, California Masonic Code,
by the Committee on Jurisprude nce on Decision No. 1 ( 1957 Proc.,
p. 368) in accord with Sec. 781. California Masonic Code. It became
the law at the close of that Communication, (Sec. 782, California
Masonic Code) and all previous decisions in conflict with it were overruled.
2. Residence in fact prescribed in said law does not mean that the
ap~lica~t must actually stay within the jurisdiction limits during the
entire time. He may be absent for short or prolonged periods on business
or oth~se, but not the whole period, so long as he intends his permanent residence to remain in said jurisdiction, provided there are some
facts to support his intention, such as:
a. Being a registered voter in said jurisdiction:
b. Holding membership in a church or club located in said jurisdiction:
c. Having an interest in a business located in said jurisdiction; or,
d. Where his parents or his family reside in said jurisdiction.
The Deputy Grand Master presiding, the Grand Master moved that
the last sentence of Section 517-s be stricken from the California
Masonic Code.
The motion was adopted by a 5/6 vote.
The report of the Jurisprude nce Committee was adopted as modified.

laws of the Territory of Hawaii. As stated by the Grand Master, it was

However, the decision is technically in violation of the section which

DEc1s10N No. 22

The Grand Master in his Decision No. 22 held that Question 15 of
the Application for Degrees embodied in 527 C.M.C. did not apply to
Square Clubs, High Twelve Clubs, social clubs, and similar social organizations which do not confer degrees and do not have formal initiation
ceremonies.
Your committee has given the subject full consideration and reports
that said question does apply to such clubs and organizations for the
following reasons:
1. 527-c provides: "The prohibition of Question 13 (now 15 )
applies to so-called 'Square Clubs' and social clubs having a prerequisite
of membership requirement." ( 1951)
2. 527-c NOTE provides in part: "Former R.D. Sec. 191 (b),
which stated that Question 13 (now 15) did not apply to purely social
clubs having no formal initiation, was repealed in 1955 (Proc. p. 362) as
having been reversed." This is clear, too, and definitely indicates that
Question 15 dou apply to such clubs.
3. 527-d provides, "Question 13 (now 15) applies to a research
group. The purpose of the 1953 Amendme nt was to insure that a new
Master Mason contributed his time and efforts to his lodge for at least a
year before expanding into other Masonic activities." ( 1955).
1. 527-f provides, "Question 13 (now 15) applies to a Masonic
Club looking toward a dispensation for a new lodge." ( 1955 ) •
5. Decision No. 17 by Grand Master L. Harold Anderson in 1957,
Proc. p. 103:
"Must a Master Mason wait one year before he is permitted to join
an organization requjring Masonic membership as a prerequisite, even
though this organizati on does not confer degrees?
"Decision : Yes. If exceptions were allowed there would be no end
to requests of this nature."
This decision was referred to the Committee on Jurisprudence: said
committee presented a resolution to Grand Lodge approving said
decisfon, which was adopted unanimou sly-1957 Proc. p. 367. Grand
Lodge even directed that said decision not be annotated in C.M.C. since
the question was long since settled and recorded in our law.

285

PROCEEDINGS OF THE

GRAND LODGE OF CALIFORNIA

6. The foregoing citations clearly indicate that Question 13 (now
15) does apply to such clubs. They represent Amendments Sec. 527
C.M.C. in accord with the requirements of Sec. 781 C.M.C. for they
were decisions of Grand Masters, ref erred to the Committee on Jurispru~
dence and reported by said committee to Grand Lodge by resolutions
which were adopted by Grand Lodge by a 5/6 vote as required by Sec.
782 C.M.C. and became the law of Grand Lodge at the close of each
respective Communication.
In his decision the Grand Master leaned too heavily upon a portion
of 527~c C.M.C .. reading as follows:
"A resolution, which stated that Question 13 (now 15) should not
apply to social organizations which do not confer degrees or have formal
initiation ceremonies, was adopted as a matter of policy in 1955 (Proc.
pp. 95, 347) but was not adopted as law." (Emphasis supplied).
Policy is not law. The italicized language in the quotation affirms
this. Said resolution was referred to the Committee on Policy only1955 Proc., 96. It was not referred to the Committee on Jurisprudence;
said Committee did not report thereon and was not passed by a 5/6 vote,
all as required by 781 and 782 C.M.C. There is nothing in our Consti~
tution or Regulations anywhere which says that a matter of policy, as
such, ever becomes law. Nor is it said that a matter of policy will con~
tradict or overrule our law. Furthermore, no resolution, policy or other~
wise, unless adopted in strict accord with the provisions of 76 and 77
or 781 and 782 C.M.C., will alter, amend or repeal our laws.
Even if we were to invoke the violent assumption that the policy
quoted above did become law when it was voted upon at the Annual
Communication in 1955, such policy was definitely repealed by the
valid adoption of 527~d~f and g C.M.C. and the repeal of R.D. Sec.
494 ( b) ( 527~c C.M.C.) at the same session, all of which became eff ec~
tive at the close of that Communication ( 782 C.M.C.) and by the valid
adoption of Decision No. 17 in 1957 Proc. p. 103, which holds that a
Master Mason must wait one ·year before he is permitted to join an
organization requiring ·Masonic membership as a prerequisite, even
though this organization does not confer degrees.
We therefore move the adoption of the following resolution:
RESOLVED: That, under the law of Grand Lodge, Question 15 of
the application ( 527 C.M.C.) does apply to Square Clubs, High Twelve
Clubs, and organizations requiring Masonic affiliation as a condition
to membership even though such organizations do not confer degrees and
do not have formal initiation ceremonies.
A motion that the decision be not approved failed of adoption.
The Deputy Grand Master presiding, the Grand Master moved that
his decision No. 22 be approved for the purpose of becoming part of our
law, and the motion was adopted by a 5/6 vote.

LIBRARY COMMISSIONERS

The Grand Master has reported that he did not appoint a Board
of Library Commissioners during the past year. This matter. and the
suggestion of the Board of Trustees of the California Masonic Memorial
Temple Corporation that a special committee or committees be appointed
to study the matter of housing a library and museum in the Memorial
Temple, has been referred to your Committee on Policy and General
Purposes.
At our Annual Communication in I 957 a resolution for the creation
of a Board of Library Commissioners, five in number, was presented and
referred to this committee. We reported in part: "We are in sympathy
with the intentions of the maker of the resolution and recommend that
the resolution to establish a Board of Library Commissioners . . . be
approved." The resolution was adopted.
It appears to your committee that the policy of having a Board of
Library Commissioners has been adopted by the Grand Lodge, and that
the matter of housing the library in the Memorial Temple and the
incidentals thereto should be referred to that board rather than to create
another special committee.
We therefore move that the action of the Grand Lodge in its 1957
Communication, establishing a Board of Library Commissioners, be
affirmed. and that the housing of the existing library and future acquisitions be referred to said board in cooperation with the Board of Trustees
of the California Masonic Memorial Temple Corporation.
Adopted.

DEDICATION OF PUBLIC SCHOOL BUILDINGS

Your Committee on Policy and General Purposes, to which has been
referred the resolution to adopt a new ceremony for the dedication of
public school buildings, reports as follows:
We understand that the main purpose of the revision of the ceremony
in line with our outspoken support of our public schools, is to emphasize
the importance of the public schools to the community and the public
welfare. It seemed to be felt by some that in our present ceremony we
were not giving adequate praise to the ideal of free public education.
It is our understanding that while this resolution seems to be sponsored by only one brother, our Grand Lecturer, it has been not only
approved. but carefully edited by the Grand Master, the Deputy Grand
Master, the Senior Grand Warden, the Junior Gra nd Warden, and the
entire Ritual Committee, and its adoption is recommended by them all.
While your Committee on Policy and Genera l Purposes does not
vouch for the authenticity of any statement made in the proposed ceremony or to its practical application, it does repose sufficient confidence
in its sponsors to recommend the adoption of the ceremony.
Your Committee on Policy and General Purposes therefore moves
the adoption of the resolution providing for a new ceremony for dedicating public school buildings and urges a " Yes" vote.
Adopted.

THE COMMITTEE ON P OLICY AND GENERAL PURPOSES:

Now brought up for consideratio n is a resolution, identified as "E",
which proposes to amend Section 203 of Ordinances by adding the
following words:
"'California Freemason' shall be mailed to each member quarterly."
The effect of the amendment will cause this publication to be distributed quarterly to every member of constituent Masonic Lodges of
California without direct charge to the individual brother.
The total cost to the fraternity will be in the neighborhoo d of eight
cents per copy. or between 30c and 35c per year. Present distribution is
in excess of 50,000 copies per issue, at a subscription price of $1.00 per
year to the individual, or 60c per year where the constituent lodge
subscribes for its total membership .
Your Committee on Policy and General Purposes recommends the
adoption of the resolution.
"California Freemason, " during its publication trial period of five
years, has proved its worth to the fraternity. Its distribution to all
members of California Lodges will bring:
1. To the "manageme nt" group of each lodge, i.e., the officers and
regular attendants, a more complete understandi ng of the objects and
activities of Masonry and the relationship of the Grand Lodge of
California to its constituent lodges.
2. To the individual Mason who is only a casual or infrequent
attendant at the meetings of his lodge, a similar understandi ng plus an
inspiration which will undoubtedly result in his more frequent attend-

GRAND LODGE OF CALIFORNIA

293

ance at the meetings of his own lodge and a more active personal participation in its affairs.
3. To the members of the brother's family. a broader understandi ng
of our order, and
4. To the non-Mason , who admittedly will read the publication or
parts thereof quite infrequently . it nevertheless will bring enlightenme nt.
The publication, in our estimation, has and will continue to have
great value to the fraternity, both within and beyond the doors of our
lodges. It has commended itself to the Grand Lodges of many other
Masonic jurisdictions , and its distribution to all members of California
lodges is extremely desirable and in the best interests of the fraternity.
Private subscription s to Masons not members of California Lodges
will be continued.
Your committee moves the adoption of the resolution and recommends a "Yes" vote.
The chairman of the Committee on Finance pointed out the amount
of additional per capita tax which would be involved if the amendment
were adopted and urged a no vote.
A majority of those present voted no.

patriotic gifts which may have no appropriate connection with Masonic
activity.
Your committee therefore respectfully recommends that Decision

AMENDMENT OF SECTION 202
COMMITTEE ON JURISPRUDENCE:
RESOLVED. That Section 202, California Masonic Code, be
amended by adding at the end thereof the following: The Commission
may omit codification of edicts and decisions which are repetitive of
matters already codified.
COMMITTEE ON POLICY AND GENERAL PURPOSES:
Your Committee on Policy and General Purposes, to which was
referred Resolution "A.'' reports as follows:
This resolution was proposed by the members of your Code Commission to omit from the annual supplements to the California Masonic
Code any edicts or decisions which are cumulative or repetitive of matters already included in the Code or a prior supplement thereto.
The merits of this proposal appear obvious: From time to time a
Grand Master is called upon to make decisions on questions submitted
to him, which decisions are frequently based upon-and repetitive ofeither the express language of sections of Masonic law or of decisions
of previous Grand Masters which were approved by Grand Lodge. It
does not seem either necessary or advisable to encumber the annual
supplements with statements which add nothing to an understanding
of what already clearly appears in the printed Code or supplements.
The Grand Lodge may be assured that the Code Commission will
carefully examine all actions and decisions made or taken at every
Annual Communication, and that the Code Commission will not fail
to see that significant actions and decisions are published for the
information of the craft in the annual supplements.
The Committee on Policy and General Purposes recommends a
"Yes" vote on Resolution "A."
Adopted 5/6 vote.

BOARDS OF RELIEF
COMMITTEE ON JURISPRUDENCE:
RESOLVED, That the title "Masonic Service Board" be substituted
for "Board of Relief' or "Boards of Relief." as applicable in Sections
153, 214, 262, 263, 264, 265, 409, 601, 602. 603, 604, and their various
annotations, of the California Masonic Code and in any other sections
of the ordinances in which the title may appear, and that all such sec~
tions be, and they are, hereby so amended.
We cannot share the view of the proposers that the word "relief"
has become repugnant.
We strongly oppose this resolution and urge that it be rejected for
the following reasons:
1. To change C.M.C. and other records in so many places would be
unnecessarily expensive.
2. Relief is among the three principal tenets of Masonry. It has
connotations of affection. The word with its implications has existed in
Masonry from time immemorial. even from the Ancient Regulations of
1721 (Art. VIL p. 355 CMC.) If something is old the indications are
that it has earned the right to live. Certainly this meaningful word
should not be abandoned in favor of the word service with its political
and commercial implications. It would appear that this is an attempt to
modernize Masonry. Modern Masonry has no place here. Masonry's
tenets, terms and roots reach into antiquity and there they must remain.
We therefore urge that the resolution be rejected.
COMMITTEE ON POLICY AND GENERAL PURPOSES :
To the Committee on Policy and General Purposes has been referred
two resolutions purporting to change the name "Board of Relief."
One of the resolutions, F-1, recommends the title "Masonic S ervice
Board" while the other, F- 2, suggests the name "Masonic Service and
Employment Bureau."
While both resolutions are based on the same arguments, the second
resolution, F-2, would not be appropriate to many existing boards that
do not have the employment service.
To members of our fraternity, the word relief has many meanings
and does not always indicate financial assistance, in fact we are informed
that less than one~third of the calls made upon these boards are requests

296

PROCEEDINGS OP THE

for funds , but in the majority of cases service is requested by the families
of sojourning brethren upon the death of the brother, and to them relief
has only one embarrassing connotation-the welfare state or the dole
which they have not asked for and do not want.
Your committee feels that this change would remove all cause for
misunderstanding and embarrassment and recommends the approval of
the resolution F~l to change the name to Masonic Service Board.

Bo.a.RD OP CONTROL:

COMMITTEE ON JURISPRUDENCE:

This refers to Resolution No. F~l referred to the Board of Control

employment bureau or function.
A majority voted against the adoption of the resolution.

By D ecision No. 17 the Grand Master held: That it is lawful for a
lodge to establish a revolving fund for use of stewards for providing
refreshments.
Your committee believes that it is not lawful for a lodge to establish
such a revolving fund for the following reasons:
1. A lodge must retain control of its own funds ( 401, California
Masonic Code).
2. The funds of a lodge are trust funds ( 409, California Masonic
Code).
3. Segregation of funds of a lodge is improper ( 409-u, California
Masonic Code).
4. Bills for refreshments and entertainment must be authorized by the
lodge before they can be paid ( 412-1, California Masonic Code).
It appears, therefore, that our law forbids entrustment of lodge
funds to the stewards.

PUBLIC SCHOOLS FUND
COMMITTEE ON JURISPRUDENCE:

COMMITTEE ON POLICY AND GENERAL PURPOSES:

On resolution of Brother Rife. your committee reports as follows:
Resolved: That Section 283 C.M.C. be amended by inserting the
following:
6th. For each Master Mason borne upon its rolls as of June 30, the
sum of 25 cents to provide a Public Schools Fund to be expended by
direction of the Grand Master for the benefit of our public schools on a
statewide basis.

Your Committee on Policy and General Purpose reports as follows
in relation to Decision No. 17 of the Grand Master.
The Grand Master held that a lodge could establish a revolving
fund for the use of the stewards in providing lodge refreshments, providing tha t expenditures from the fund be submitted monthly for
approval by the lodge. and tha t the fund should never be larger than
the estimated monthly requirement.
The establishment of a revolving fund is a segregation of lodge funds
and setting aside a portion thereof for expenditure for a future event.
This would appear to be contrary to the provisions of Section 409-u
of C.M.C.
There is no question that in some instances the use of a revolving
fu nd for the steward s may be a convenience. Your committee, however,
is of the opinion that such convenience does not outweigh Masonic law
and customs, and that many problems might arise under such a plan
which would be embarrassing to the lodge and to the stewards.
We, therefore, move the approval of Decision 17 of the Grand
Master and recommend a "No" vote.
A motion to approve the decision was not adopted.

COMMITTEE ON Poucy AND GENERAL PURPOSES:

To your Committee on Policy and General Purposes was referred
the resolution resolving that this Grand Lodge establish a fund to be
known as "Our Public Schools Fund," and that a twenty-five cent per
capita tax be imposed for this purpose; and that the Grand Master
appoint a committee to disperse from said fund for the protection of
our public schools on a sta tewide basis.
We feel that this is in keeping with the policy already adop ted by
Grand Lodge, and that in order to meet problems pertaining to our
public schools which may arise in the future, such a fund should be
available for that purpose.
Your committee therefore recommends the adoption of this resolution.

DECISION No. 20
COMMITTEE ON JURISPRUDENCE:

With reference to the Grand Master's Decision No. 20, your Committee on Jurisprudence reports as follows:
Before applying for our degrees the applicant pleaded guilty to a
charge of stealing an automobile in Missouri, and was sentenced to a
term of two years in the Missouri State prison, and was confined therein
for a few days.
Thereafter two other men charged with the same offense were tried
and acquitted. From the facts developed on this trial, it became clearly
a~parent that applicant was not and could not have been guilty of the
crime. To rectify this miscarriage of justice the Missouri courts set
aside the judgment, and the man was released from prison. Thereafter,
the governor of Missouri granted a full pardon.
Section 511 , C.M.C., provides that one who has served a term in a
state or federal prison is not under the tongue of good report and is.
therefore. ineligible to membership in our fraternity . (Sub. h, Sec. 511.)
In this case the judgment was a nullity, and the Missouri courts
declared that applicant was guilty of no crime. Therefore, the reason
for the rule ceases.
We agree with the 1Grand Master, and move the following resolution:
RESOLVED. That Grand Master's ruling No. 20 be, and the same
is, hereby approved.
Committee on Policy and General Purposes reported their concurrence.
Unanimously adopted.

GRAND MASTER's RECOMMENDATION No. 3
Committe e on Jurisprudence:
By Recomme ndation No. 3 it appears that the Grand Master recommends:
That Section 346. California Masonic Code, be amended by inserting in the third line thereof, between the words "fee" and "shall.'' the
following:
and all of his previous contributi ons
Your committee urges rejection for the following reasons.
Forfeiture is a drastic process denoting a penalty which should
never be invoked by our fraternity against non-Maso ns except upon the
basis of sure and ample justice. There is some justice in our present
law which requires forfeiture of fees by an applicant who will never be a
Mason. because the lodge has devoted some efforts and has been put to
some expense as a result of his applicatio n.
However, there is no justice at all in forcing an applicant, who is not
a Mason and never will be a Mason. to forfeit his forced contributi ons
for the benefit of our Masonic Homes. George Washingt on Masonic
National Memorial and our Masonic Memorial Temple, which the
applicant will never have the privilege of using or enjoying. Our lodges
should never demand something for nothing. This would be denying
the benefits and enforcing the burdens.
COMMITTEE ON Poucv AND GENERAL PURPOSES:
That legislation be adopted to supplemen t Section 346 C.M.C. to the
end that where fee of a candidate is forfeited, contributi ons also be
forfeited.
Without regard to particular sections of the California Masonic
Code, we recommen d that it be the policy of Grand Lodge that where fee
is forfeited that contributi ons also be forfeited and that legislation pursuant thereto be adopted.
A majority voted no on the adoption of the recommen dation.
AMENDMENT OF SECTION 681-b
Committe e on Jurisprudence:
Resolution by Brother Albert F. Ross seeks to repeal 681-b C.M.C.
This section provides in part: "Acts committed before initiation ... if
in themselve s wrong or immoral they may be punished afterward ."
No reasons are assigned for such repeal. This section has been the
law of Grand Lodge for 88 years and it should not be repealed just for
the sake of repeal. To repeal it could mean that, once a man has become
a Mason, no past offense, however heinous, could alfect his status. This
would be positively harmful.

DECISION No. 27
Committe e on furisprude nce:
The Grand Master ruled that posting garish placards and signs on
the outside of a Masonic Temple by one who has rented it for the purpose of giving lectures on "faith healing" is a use and practice inconsistent with the dignity of Freemaso nry. He also held that Temple
Associatio ns and Lodges should exercise careful control over the advertising methods of tenants and the uses to which Temple properties are
put by appropria te rental agreement s.
This decision is consistent with accepted Masonic practices and is
in accord with our law.
Section 401 of our Masonic Code provides that a Lodge must retain
control over its properties . Annotatio n b. thereof provides that a Lodge
may rent its hall to others.
The general provisions of our laws, too numerous to here mention,
together with long establishe d custom. proscribe any activity which may
bring discredit on the Craft or its property.
The Grand Master's decision is approved.
The Committe e on Policy and General Purposes report their concurrence.
Adopted.

USE OF VISUAL AIDS
The Gra nd Lecturer a nnounced that the Ritual Committee had considered the matter of visual aids and had come to the following conclusions :
In accordance w ith the indicated desire of the majority in Grand
Lodge. and effective immediately, it will be permissible for officers to call
attention to any of the monitorial emblems by appropriate gestures (but
without diverting attention of the candidate from the lecture). This will
apply to a chart or scroll exhibiting only monitorial emblems, as well as
to physical representa tio ns. which may be of moderate size only. In
lodges desiring to ma ke use of such monitoria l representations, however,
it will be mandatory for the officers to learn, qualify in and give those
portions of the lectures covering the monitorial emblems.
The lodges will also be permitted to make use of a ceiling light
above the altar.

REPORT OF COMMITTEE ON SOJOURNERS
To the Most Worshipful Grand Lodge of California:
The committee on sojourners this past year has directed its efforts
toward encouraging the lodges of the Grand Jurisdiction to set up
sojourners committees in each lodge, whose purpose was to give thought
to and take action on the problems of sojourners. It is recognized that
there may be as many sojourning brethren in C alifornia as there are
members of the jurisdiction. The aim of your grand lodge committee has
been to get these "outside" brethren to attend Masonic Blue Lodge
functions, not only to encourage their affiliation, but to get them to
participate in some phase of the fraternity's activity. It is felt that too
many members are only dues-payers, and as a consequence miss much
of the fraternity 's significance. This problem is one of education at the
lodge level. with the ultimate objective being a functioning sojourners
committee in each lodge. Once this is recognized by all, we believe that
such committees can ably discharge the responsibilities of the Grand
Lodge to the sojourners in our midst.
Some lodges have greater opportunities for work among sojourners
than others. Many lodges schedule dinners, dances, family nights,
Masonic education programs and other functions especially for sojourners. Other lodges, for va rious reasons, do little along these lines. It is
the latter group which requires our encouragement and assistance. In
response to a questionnaire recently sent to all masters, the following
figures were obtained: Out of 684 mailed, 270 were returned. Of this
number, 197 lodges had active sojourners committees, 120 had scheduled
special nights, while 145 masters felt their committees had made positive
accomplishments. Some have suggested tha t the $25.00 Homes Endowment Fee be dropped from the affilia tion charge to render it more a ttractive financially for those interested in joining. This suggestion has been
made in the past but has never been received favorably as it is felt that
all members of California lodges should make this contribution. However, your committee encourages lodges to lower their own affiliation
cha rge to a token minimum amount.
At the request of the Grand Secretary, your committee considered
a proposition from a sojourning past mas ter from Indiana, now living
in San Diego. This brother wishes, by means of a registration questionnaire mailed out to sojourners in the area, to establis h a sojourners blood
bank and encourage the brethren to attend Masonic funerals and visit
the sick. He has received encouragement from the loca l Board of Relief,
with whom he intends to coordinate his activities. This would be a
voluntary service, carried on at his own expense, with no solicitation

307

PROCEEDINGS OF THE

GRAND LODGE OF CALIFORNIA

for funds. Although this project would probably have no direct results
in bringing about affiliations from out-of-state Masons, it could locate
or uncover potential prospects. As this sojourner has been working
closely with the Board of Relief in San Diego on a seemingly worthwhile
idea, your committee feels this brother should be encouraged in his
program.
The annual reports show that over the past several years an average
of about 2.500 affiliates were elected to California lodges yearly. Of this
number, 909 in 1956, 898 in 1957, and 829 in 1958, were from out of
the state. Realizing that we have an average yearly gain of slightly
over 4.000 members, we see that the out-of-state affiliates bring us
approximately 20 per cent of this figure.
Plans for next year include a booklet-type guide dealing with the
sojourners problem. This would go to every master giving him suggested
procedures, proposed events for attracting sojourners. and questions and
answers most commonly raised. With the progress that has been made
in the past in connection with sojourners and their affiliation with local
lodges and the work that is still to be done in the future with the neverending entrance of Masons to this state, your committee urges the continuance of effort and interest on the part of all the constituent lodges.
Your chairmen wish to express their thanks to the Grand Master,
and other Grand Lodge officers a s well as the individual committee members for their support and cooperation. It has been a privilege and a
pleasure to serve Grand Lodge this past year.
Fraternally.
WILLIAM A . CoHENDET, Northern Chairman
FRED G. DOAN, Southern Chairman

REPORT OF SPECIAL COMMITTEE ON
OLD MASONIC HALL AT LOS ANGELES
To the Most Worshipful Grand Lodge F. & A. M. of California:
We refer you to previous reports of this committee for information
relating to circumstances surrounding this first Masonic Hall in Los
Angeles.
We are pleased to report that on September 8 the City Council of
Los Angeles approved the sale to the State of California of the property
at 416 .Yi North M ain Street, on which the old hall is loca ted.
The approval included instructions to the City Attorney to present
to the Council the necessary ordinance authorizing the sale of the
property to the State of California. The opinion has been expressed that
the adoption of the ordinance and the eventual transfer of title to the
State will now be a routine procedure. When these steps are completed,
the old Hall becomes a part of the master plan for the Pueblo de Los
Angeles State Historical Monument. W e are informed that State funds
for restoration of the building have been allocated, a nd with completion
of architectural and structural drawings the work will commence.
No expense has been incurred by the committee and we do not anticipate any for the immediate future. We recommend the continuation of

REPORT OF THE COMMITTEE ON RITUAL
PERAMBULATION RITUAL

We have carefully considered the resolution of certain brethren of
the 620th Masonic District Officers' Association, proposing that "the
perambulations during degree work be a portion of the duties of the
Senior Deacon."
If this language be taken literally, it is already the duty of the
Senior Deacon to conduct the candidate. However, we assume that what
is meant is that the Senior Deacon should give the scripture recital
during perambulation.
The ruling in this respect has heretofore been that the Senior Deacon
might give this, as might any other brother designated by the Master,
but it has been recommended that the Senior Deacon should not give it.
In our opinion, the adoption of the proposal would not add anything
to the dignity of the work nor be any more impressive to the candidate.
It would materially add to the memorized work of an officer who already
has much to do and much to learn in order to become proficient. Furthermore, it would take away the opportunity for one or more other brethren
to actively participate in the work.
Another important consideration is that in a large number of lodges,
particularly metropolitan lodges, this part is sung by vocalists. To
require the Senior Deacon to give the recitals would eliminate this very
pleasing musical addition.
We recommend that the resolution be not adopted.
ELBERT

w. DAVIS

CLARE B. CAMPBELL
RALPH M. F OOTE
ARTHUR

J. KAHN

RAYMOND G. TAYLOR
DONALD G. TAYLOR

w. B E N SORRELLS

PAST MASTERS' APRONS

There has been presented a resolution to permit Past Masters to
wear their Past Masters' aprons when engaged in degree work.
No one ca n engage in degree work as a matter of right, without
permission of the Master of the lodge, who may invite qualified breth-

GRAND LODGE OP CALIFORNIA

PROCEEDINGS OP THE

312

ren to assist in conferring a degree. The conferring of the degree is
for the benefit of the candidate, however, and not for the display of
honors attained by the man who is doing the work. We therefore can
see no reason why a Past Master should engage in degree work under
any other conditions than one who is not a Past Master, or why he
should not wear the regalia of the officer whose station or place he is
occupying.
We recommend that the resolution be not adopted.
The resolution failed of adoption.

REPORT OF COMMITTE E ON FINANCE
To the Most Worshipful Grand Lodge F. 6 A. M. of California:

In accordance with the provision of Ordinances, the firm of Skinner
and Hammond has audited all accounts of Grand Lodge, the Masonic
Homes, and the Memorial Temple for the fiscal year ended June 30,
1958. These reports have been examined and it is our opinion that they
correctly present the financial condition of these activities.
The audit shows total revenue for the support of Grand Lodge of
$341,911.76, and expenses and appropriations of $296,842,79, leaving a
balance of unexpended revenue of $45,068.97. In addition, Grand Lodge
received $21 ,999.96 as reimbursement from the Masonic H omes for
Salary and Endowment Board expense, making a total of $67,068.93.
which has been transferred to Capital Account.
It should be noted, however, that of this $67,000.00 surplus, approximately $58,000.00 is represented by unexpended appropriations for
Employees Retirement Plan and Temple Dedication, and a net gain from
the operation of " California Freemason." The latter amount should be
set up as a fund against magazine subscriptions paid in advance, and
the Pension Plan and Temple Dedication expenses have been included
again in the budget for the current fiscal year.
Your committee commends all boards , committees, and those in
charge of administration for their efforts in holding expenses well within
budgeted appropriations .
GRAND TREASURER'S REPORT

We have examined the Grand Treasurer's report, which was referred
to this committee. All items of income and expenditure, as well as funds
on hand and investment portfolio, are in accord with the audit. The
report has our entire approval.
We particularly note his recommendatio n that a definite per capita
be set aside each year to be added to the reserves of Grand Lodge. This
committee, in reporting last year, stated that when the current period of
non-recurring high expenses is behind us, Grand Lodge should make a
serious effort to spend substantially less than it takes in and add to its
reserves each year. At such a time the committee will give consideration
of putting into effect the recommendatio n of the Grand Treasurer.
EX CESS EXPENDITURES OVER BUDGETED AMOUNTS

There has been referred to this committee that portion of the Grand
Master's Message in which he reported approval by him of expenditures
in excess of items in the budget totaling for the last fiscal year the
relatively small sum of $2.371,83, made up largely of one item for
$1 .855.85 covering unforeseen costs in Grand Lodge litigation. We
recommend approval of the action of the Grand Master.
CORRESPONDEN CE COMMITTEE-"C ALIPORNIA FREEMASON"

cation of our official magazine, "California Freemason," in the last fiscal

However, these funds are more than offset by receipts from advance
subscriptions which, in regular accounting practice, would be carried
as a liability. Heretofore no action has been taken in this respect, but

Grand Secretary by $1.000.00, which will bring it to $11.000.00 per

of these offices. and it is only just and fair that a corresponding increase
in compensation should be made. It bears repeating that the efficiency

MASONIC HOMES

The Finance Committee has reviewed the audit of the accounts of the
Masonic Homes of California and the report of the Trustees. We have
consulted the Board to ascertain their estimate of the funds needed
to support the operation of the Homes for the current fiscal year. Your
chairman was permitted to attend a full meeting of the Board, at which
plans were reviewed for the extensive, costly, and muchly needed
building program at Decoto to be commenced in the near future.
While the Board feels that a renewal of the per capita tax of $.50
will be sufficient for the current fiscal year. it should be noted that in
another year the Homes will probably not be able to make ends meet
with income based on this per capita. They face the loss of investment
income derived from capital funds which will be spent on the building
program at Decato, and the probability of a substantial increase in operating expense resulting from higher wages.
We offer the following resolution:
RESOLVED, that the sum of $.50 per capita be levied for the fiscal
year ending June 30, 1959. the proceeds to be paid to the Trustees of
the Masonic Homes.
BUDGET

In presenting the budget for the current fiscal year ending June 30,
1959, special attention is directed to several items.
SALARIES

For some years it has been the accounting procedure to carry the
budgeted appropriation for salaries at the net cost to Grand Lodge after
crediting the amount paid to Grand Lodge by the Masonic Homes for
services rendered to the Homes by the Grand Secretary and Assistant
Grand Secretary.
On the recommendation of our auditors we are changing the procedure to show salaries at the total amount disbursed by Grand Lodge,

MEMORIAL TEMPLE

In the budget for the first quarter of the current fiscal year adopted
at the 1957 Grand Lodge Communication there was included $10,000.00
for expense of the Memorial Temple dedication. This is in addition to
$5,000.00 provided for the same purpose in the previous fiscal year.
Only $342.65 of this $5,000.00 appropriation was expended, the remainder being transferred to Capital Account as previously noted.
After consultation with those in charge of the dedication program, we
estimate the total cost for this fiscal year at $20,000.00 and have set up
this amount in the budget. It includes. of course, the $10,000.00 previously appropriated for the first quarter. We have been conservative in
our estimate, but no accurate figure can be given until all bills are in.
We trust that this appropriation will be sufficient.
RETIREMENT PENSION PLAN FOR GRAND LODGE EMPLOYEES

As previously noted, no disbursement was made during the last
fiscal year of the $19 ,500.00 budgeted for Retirement Pension Plan of
Grand Lodge employees. except for $250.00 paid for actuary service.
Action has been delayed pending amendment of the Trust Agreement
and the Retirement Income Plan of Masonic Homes of California and
the approval by the Internal Revenue Service.
We anticipate that these matters will be cleared in the current year.
Our actuaries advise us that approximately $38,000.00 will be required
to cover all costs from January 1. 1956, the established effective date for
these employees, to the end of the current fiscal year.
There has been previously set aside in a special bank account $22,~
753.91 for this purpose. We are budgeting $16,000.00 which, together
with the funds in the special account. will bring the total to the amount
required. Our auditors suggest that Grand Lodge approval be given
to the appropriation of $22,753.91 set aside in the special bank account
for Grand Lodge Employees Retirement Pension Plan. these funds to

be transferred to the current Administrative and Office Expense budget
and paid out for this purpose as required. We recommend approval of

CAPITAL ADDITIONS AND REPLA CEMENTS

At the 1957 Annual Communication a new section was added to the
budget entitled "Capital Additions and Replacements," under which all
amounts expended for furnishings and equipment which become the
property of Grand Lodge are capitalized and carried on the balance sheet
as an asset.
There was budgeted for this purpse in the last fi scal year $33.796.76.
The audit report shows $35.656.83 expended, the items purchased being
listed and carried on the balance sheet as an asset.
For the current fi scal year we have budgeted under this section
$4 .500.00. This will cover the balance due on the offset printing press,
which is a valuable addition to the office equipment, and some small
items of equipment, all of which are detailed in the budget.

ANNUAL ELECTION
The Grand Master announced that the hour had arrived for the
Annual Election and directed the Grand Secretary to read the Sections
of the Constitution applying to the same.
The R. W . Phil N. Myers, McCloud Lodge No. 430, was elected
Grand Master.
The R. W. Joe L. Shell, San Diego Lodge No. 35, was elected
Deputy Grand Master.
The R. W . Alfred F. Breslauer. Starr King Lodge No. 344, was
elected Senior Grand Warden

Grand W arden.

No. 560, was re-elected G rand Treasurer.
The M. W . Lloyd E. Wilson, P ast Grand Master, Ingleside Lodge
No. 630, was re-elected Grand Secretary.
The V. W. Elbert W . Davis, Francis K. Shattuck Lodge No. 571.
was re-elected Grand Lecturer.

names of the appointive officers as follows:

PROCEEDINGS OP THE

Grand Organist, Harold Mueller, California Lodge No. 1.
Grand Tiler, David Wright, Menlo Park Lodge No. 651.
The Grand Secretary announced the re-appointment by the Grand
Master elect of Past Grand Masters Edward H. Siems and Frank
Harwell, Jr. as Trustees of the California Masonic Memorial Temple.
The Grand Secretary also announced the appointment by the Grand
Master elect of Trustees of the Masonic Homes as follows:
Past Grand Master Leo E. Anderson for the un-expired term of
Guy B. Mize (Junior Grand Warden), Past Grand Master Edgar
V. Stewart, Jr. to succeed Myron E. Smith (eligibility expired), and
Past Grand Master Harold L. Anderson to succeed Past Grand Master
Charles Albert Adams (eligibility expired).

INSTALLATION OF OFFICERS
The Most Worshipful Ellsworth Meyer, Past Grand Master acted
as Master of Ceremonies , and the officers, elected and appointed, with
the exception of Ogden D. Pinkerton, Junior Grand Steward, were installed by the retiring Grand Master in accordance with the Ritual.
The newly installed Grand Master invested his predecessor with a
Past Grand Master's lapel button.
The Charles Albert Adams insignia was transferred from the retiring to the incumbent Grand Master, and the other chair officers exchanged the Arthur S. Crites lapel pins.
The J. Everett Houser lapel pin was transferred from the retiring
to the incumbent Grand Orator
Past Grand Master Arthur M . Warren, who had originally presented the Grand Tiler's lapel insignia to Alvin A. Horwege, presented
it to the newly installed Grand Tiler, David Wright.
The Most Worshipful Edward H. Siems, Past Grand Master, invested the retiring Grand Master with the apron of his new designation
and with a gift to be tendered to Mrs. Anderson from the members of
Grand Lodge. The Jr. Past Grand Master acknowledged both presentations in his typically courteous manner.
At 5:00 p.m.. all business being completed, Grand Lodge was closed
in due form.

Temple site real property and the improvements thereon and ere to
be further secured by a chattel mortgage on the !urnishinga and
equipnent of' the mnt Temple, The notes are repayable in annual
instalments of' $20,000 to each bank beginning October l, 1958,
and continuing annually thereafter until October .l, 1965, on
which latter date all sums of' principal and interest then unpaid
shall be due · and payable, The notes bear interest at the rate of'
4% per annwu, payable semi..,.nnuall,y April 1st and Octooer lat of

continued.
